question: Does a phone buzz cost attention even when its owner never looks at the phone?
answer: Yes. People doing a dull attention task made more errors after their phone buzzed or chimed with a message, even though they did not touch it, and the drop was comparable to that seen in people who actually read or answered. The alert alone starts the mind drafting a reply.
move: An alert you ignore still takes a slice of attention.
ask: Which alerts on my phone could I switch off today without missing anything that matters?
reference: Stothart, Mitchum & Yehnert, The attentional cost of receiving a cell phone notification, Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance, 2015
